        has_epilogue_fusion: Bool,
    ](
        res: FusedOutputTensor,
        a: InputTensor,
        b: InputTensor,
        ctx: DeviceContext,
    ) raises:
        pass


@extensibility.register("map_lower_scalar")
struct MapLowerScalar:
    @staticmethod
    def execute[
        dtype: DType,
        target: StaticString,
    ](
        res: OutputTensor,
        a: InputTensor,
        s: Scalar[dtype],
        ctx: DeviceContext,
    ) raises:
        pass


@extensibility.register("map_lower_variadic")
struct MapLowerVariadic:
    @staticmethod
    def execute[
        dtype: DType,
        size: Int,
        target: StaticString,
    ](
        res: OutputTensor,
        inputs: InputVariadicTensors[dtype=dtype, rank=1, size=size, ...],
        ctx: DeviceContext,
    ) raises:
        pass


# A real-body counterpart to `map_lower_one_plain_output`: same plain-output
# signature (so it lowers through the identical MAP plain path), but it actually
# writes `res = a + 1` so an end-to-end run can validate a numeric result.
@extensibility.register("map_lower_add_one")
struct MapLowerAddOne:
    @staticmethod
    def execute[
        target: StaticString,
    ](res: OutputTensor, a: InputTensor, ctx: DeviceContext,) raises:
        @inline(.always)
        def func[width: Int](idx: Coord) {var} -> SIMD[res.dtype, width]:
            return rebind[SIMD[res.dtype, width]](a.load[width](idx)) + 1

        foreach[target=target](func, res, ctx)


# Real-body plain-output kernels below broaden the advanced-fusion MAP-ABI
# execution coverage past the single 1-in/1-out shape. Each mirrors
# `map_lower_add_one`: a plain `OutputTensor` (no epilogue fusion) driven by a
# real `foreach` closure, so the MAP plain path both lowers AND computes a
# deterministic result an end-to-end run can validate. Output shape is
# identity-from-first-input for all of them, so none needs a shape function.


# 3 inputs / 1 output: `res = a + b + c`.
@extensibility.register("map_lower_add3")
struct MapLowerAdd3:
    @staticmethod
    def execute[
        target: StaticString,
    ](
        res: OutputTensor,
        a: InputTensor,
        b: InputTensor,
        c: InputTensor,
        ctx: DeviceContext,
    ) raises:
        @inline(.always)
        def func[width: Int](idx: Coord) {var} -> SIMD[res.dtype, width]:
            return (
                rebind[SIMD[res.dtype, width]](a.load[width](idx))
                + rebind[SIMD[res.dtype, width]](b.load[width](idx))
                + rebind[SIMD[res.dtype, width]](c.load[width](idx))
            )

        foreach[target=target](func, res, ctx)


# 1 input / 2 outputs: `res0 = a + 1`, `res1 = a * 2` (two plain outputs, two
# independent `foreach` loops).
@extensibility.register("map_lower_two_outputs")
struct MapLowerTwoOutputs:
    @staticmethod
    def execute[
        target: StaticString,
    ](
        res0: OutputTensor,
        res1: OutputTensor,
        a: InputTensor,
        ctx: DeviceContext,
    ) raises:
        @inline(.always)
        def add_one[width: Int](idx: Coord) {var} -> SIMD[res0.dtype, width]:
            return rebind[SIMD[res0.dtype, width]](a.load[width](idx)) + 1

        foreach(add_one, res0, ctx)

        @inline(.always)
        def times_two[width: Int](idx: Coord) {var} -> SIMD[res1.dtype, width]:
            return rebind[SIMD[res1.dtype, width]](a.load[width](idx)) * 2

        foreach(times_two, res1, ctx)


# 2 inputs / 2 outputs: `res0 = a + b`, `res1 = a - b`.
@extensibility.register("map_lower_add_sub")
struct MapLowerAddSub:
    @staticmethod
    def execute[
        target: StaticString,
    ](
        res0: OutputTensor,
        res1: OutputTensor,
        a: InputTensor,
        b: InputTensor,
        ctx: DeviceContext,
    ) raises:
        @inline(.always)
        def add[width: Int](idx: Coord) {var} -> SIMD[res0.dtype, width]:
            return rebind[SIMD[res0.dtype, width]](a.load[width](idx)) + rebind[
                SIMD[res0.dtype, width]
            ](b.load[width](idx))

        foreach[target=target](add, res0, ctx)

        @inline(.always)
        def sub[width: Int](idx: Coord) {var} -> SIMD[res1.dtype, width]:
            return rebind[SIMD[res1.dtype, width]](a.load[width](idx)) - rebind[
                SIMD[res1.dtype, width]
            ](b.load[width](idx))

        foreach[target=target](sub, res1, ctx)


# Scalar operand: `res = a * s` where `s: Scalar[dtype]`. Exercises the MAP
# `scalar.create` materialization path with a real computed result.
@extensibility.register("map_lower_scale")
struct MapLowerScale:
    @staticmethod
    def execute[
        dtype: DType,
        target: StaticString,
    ](
        res: OutputTensor[dtype=dtype, ...],
        a: InputTensor[dtype=dtype, ...],
        s: Scalar[dtype],
        ctx: DeviceContext,
    ) raises:
        @inline(.always)
        def func[width: Int](idx: Coord) {var} -> SIMD[res.dtype, width]:
            return rebind[SIMD[res.dtype, width]](a.load[width](idx)) * rebind[
                Scalar[res.dtype]
            ](s)

        foreach(func, res, ctx)


# Variadic operand: `res = sum(inputs)` over an `InputVariadicTensors`.
# Exercises the MAP `tuple.create` materialization path. Modeled on the
# signature-only `map_lower_variadic` but with a real summing body.
@extensibility.register("map_lower_var_sum")
struct MapLowerVarSum:
    @staticmethod
    def execute[
        dtype: DType,
        size: Int,
        target: StaticString,
    ](
        res: OutputTensor[dtype=dtype, rank=1, ...],
        inputs: InputVariadicTensors[dtype=dtype, rank=1, size=size, ...],
        ctx: DeviceContext,
    ) raises:
        @inline(.always)
        def func[width: Int](idx: Coord) {var} -> SIMD[res.dtype, width]:
            var acc = SIMD[res.dtype, width](0)

            comptime for i in range(size):
                acc += rebind[SIMD[res.dtype, width]](
                    inputs[i].load[width](idx)
                )

            return acc

        foreach(func, res, ctx)


@extensibility.register("map_lower_two_fused_inputs")
struct MapLowerTwoFusedInputs:
    @staticmethod
    def execute[
        target: StaticString,
    ](
        res: OutputTensor,
        a: FusedInputTensor,
        b: FusedInputTensor,
        ctx: DeviceContext,
    ) raises:
        pass


@extensibility.register("map_lower_partial_fused_inputs")
struct MapLowerPartialFusedInputs:
    @staticmethod
    def execute[
        target: StaticString,
    ](
        res: OutputTensor,
        a: FusedInputTensor,
        b: InputTensor,
        ctx: DeviceContext,
    ) raises:
        pass


# `trait_tensor_tuple_fused_concat` through a host-built unified closure: the
# host projects the whole tuple to its access-enabled views with
# `TensorTuple._fused_view(inputs)`, the device closure copy-captures the view
# tuple, and the body loads element `k` through it. The view tuple is
# `RegisterPassable` only conditionally, which the closure emitter proves from
# the tuple's bindings. GPU only.
@extensibility.register("trait_tensor_tuple_fused_concat_unified_closure")
struct TraitTensorTupleFusedConcatUnifiedClosure:
    @staticmethod
    def execute[
        Ins: TypeList[Trait=Input & Fused & LoadAccess, ...],
        //,
        target: StaticString,
    ](
        z: Some[Output & TileTensorable],
        inputs: TensorTuple[*Ins],
        ctx: DeviceContext,
    ) raises:
        comptime if is_cpu[target]():
            raise Error(
                "trait_tensor_tuple_fused_concat_unified_closure only runs on"
                " the GPU"
            )
        else:
            comptime assert conforms_to(type_of(z), TileTensorable)
            var zt = z.to_tile_tensor()
            comptime out_dtype = type_of(zt).dtype
            var offsets = StaticTuple[Int32, len(Ins) + 1](fill=0)
            comptime for k in range(len(Ins)):
                offsets[k + 1] = offsets[k] + Int32(
                    Int(inputs[k].shape().product())
                )
            var n_dev = offsets[len(Ins)]
            var views = TensorTuple._fused_view(inputs)

            def device_body() {var views, var zt, var offsets, var n_dev}:
                var i = Int32(global_idx.x)
                if i >= n_dev:
                    return
                comptime for k in range(len(Ins)):
                    if i >= offsets[k] and i < offsets[k + 1]:
                        comptime assert conforms_to(type_of(views[k]), Loadable)
                        zt.reshape(row_major(Int(n_dev))).store(
                            (Int(i),),
                            views[k]
                            .load[1]((Int(i - offsets[k]),))
                            .cast[out_dtype](),
                        )

            comptime block_size = 64
            ctx.enqueue_function(
                device_body,
                grid_dim=(ceildiv(Int(n_dev), block_size),),
                block_dim=(block_size,),
            )


# A kernel with two `execute` overloads under one registration
# (`supports_unfused_execute`). The graph compiler calls the fused one when
# any output has a fused epilogue, with an identity epilogue on the others, and
# the plain one when none has, so the kernel keeps a direct store path without
# branching on `has_epilogue_fusion`. The plain overload needs its `where`
# clause: a fused output wrapper is a `Tensor` too, and Mojo does not rank the
# fused overload's bound as more specific. `z` is `x + 1` through either
# overload; `w` records which ran: 1 fused, 0 plain.
@extensibility.register("trait_unfused_execute")
struct TraitUnfusedExecute:
    @staticmethod
    def execute[
        target: StaticString,
    ](
        z: Some[Output & Fused & StoreAccess],
        w: Some[Output & Fused & StoreAccess],
        x: Some[Input & Tensor],
        ctx: DeviceContext,
    ) raises:
        comptime assert (
            type_of(x).rank == 1
            and type_of(z).rank == 1
            and type_of(w).rank == 1
        )
        comptime if is_cpu[target]():
            comptime assert conforms_to(type_of(x), TileTensorable)
            comptime assert conforms_to(type_of(z), Storable)
            comptime assert conforms_to(type_of(w), Storable)
            var xt = x.to_tile_tensor()
            for i in range(Int(xt.dim[0]())):
                var raw = rebind[SIMD[type_of(z).dtype, 1]](xt.load((i,))) + 1
                z.store[1](Coord(i), raw)
                w.store[1](Coord(i), SIMD[type_of(w).dtype, 1](1))
        else:
            raise Error("trait_unfused_execute is CPU-only")

    @staticmethod
    def execute[
        target: StaticString,
    ](
        z: Some[Output & Tensor],
        w: Some[Output & Tensor],
        x: Some[Input & Tensor],
        ctx: DeviceContext,
    ) raises where not conforms_to(type_of(z), Fused):
        comptime assert (
            type_of(x).rank == 1
            and type_of(z).rank == 1
            and type_of(w).rank == 1
        )
        comptime if is_cpu[target]():
            comptime assert conforms_to(type_of(x), TileTensorable)
            comptime assert conforms_to(type_of(z), TileTensorable)
            comptime assert conforms_to(type_of(w), TileTensorable)
            var xt = x.to_tile_tensor()
            var zt = z.to_tile_tensor()
            var wt = w.to_tile_tensor()
            for i in range(Int(xt.dim[0]())):
                var raw = rebind[SIMD[type_of(zt).dtype, 1]](xt.load((i,))) + 1
                zt.store((i,), raw)
                wt.store((i,), SIMD[type_of(wt).dtype, 1](0))
        else:
            raise Error("trait_unfused_execute is CPU-only")

// RUN: mo-opt %s --pass-pipeline='builtin.module(mogg-import-packages, mo-to-map, map-outline-structured-kernel-bodies, mo.graph(map-livm, map.iter.opaque(canonicalize)), map-to-mogg)' | FileCheck %s

// Full pipeline from a real mo.static.broadcast_to op through MOToMAP,
// outlining, view motion, and MAPToMOGG: map.index.broadcast.stride lowers to
// mogg.tensor.create.broadcast, which only carries the view's own output
// shape -- the input's shape/rank is read off the input tensor operand at
// Mojo-emission time, not duplicated onto this op. The `canonicalize` right
// after LoopInvariantViewMotion drops the closure's now-dead original input
// capture (unused once the hoisted broadcast view replaces the load) via
// `DropDeadCapturingClosureCaptures`.

// Rank-preserving: in-shape dim 0 (size 1) broadcasts to 8.

// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @broadcastSameRank
// CHECK:       [[KERNEL:%[^ ]+]] = mogg.routine ({{.*}} : !mo.tensor<[1, 64], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[8, 64], f32>
// CHECK-NEXT:  inputs ([[IP:%[^ :,]+]])
// CHECK-NEXT:  outputs ([[OP:%[^ :,]+]])
// CHECK-NEXT:  context ([[CTX:%[^ :,]+]]) attributes {device = #M.device_ref<"cpu", 0>, fusionInfo = {{.*}}} {
// CHECK-NEXT:    [[ISH:%[^ ]+]] = mogg.shape.create() <shape = #mosh<ape[1, 64]> : !mosh.ape>
// CHECK-NEXT:    [[IT:%[^ ]+]] = mogg.tensor.create([[IP]], [[ISH]]) {{.*}}io = Input{{.*}} : !mogg.tensor
// CHECK-NEXT:    [[OSH:%[^ ]+]] = mogg.shape.create() <shape = #mosh<ape[8, 64]> : !mosh.ape>
// CHECK-NEXT:    [[OT:%[^ ]+]] = mogg.tensor.create([[OP]], [[OSH]]) {{.*}}io = Output{{.*}} : !mogg.tensor
// CHECK-NEXT:    [[BCAST:%[^ ]+]] = mogg.tensor.create.broadcast([[IT]]) {{.*}}outShape = #mosh<ape[8, 64]>{{.*}} : !mogg.tensor
// CHECK-NEXT:    [[LSH:%[^ ]+]] = mogg.shape.create() <shape = #mosh<ape[8, 64]> : !mosh.ape>
// CHECK-NEXT:    mogg.call.foreach @builtin_primitives.primitives._foreach shape([[LSH]]) context([[CTX]]) ([[IDX:%[^ :,]+]] : !map.index<2>) capturing {[[OUT:%[^ :,]+]] = [[OT]] : !mogg.tensor, [[BCASTARG:%[^ :,]+]] = [[BCAST]] : !mogg.tensor} device = "cpu" {
// CHECK-NEXT:      [[VAL:%[^ ]+]] = mogg.tensor.load [[BCASTARG]]{{\[}}[[IDX]]] : !mogg.tensor, !map.index<2> -> !mogg.simd<f32>
// CHECK-NEXT:      mogg.tensor.store [[OUT]]{{\[}}[[IDX]]] = [[VAL]] : !mogg.tensor, !map.index<2>, !mogg.simd<f32>
// CHECK-NEXT:    }
// CHECK-NEXT:  }
mo.graph @broadcastSameRank(%input: !mo.tensor<[1, 64], f32>)
    -> !mo.tensor<[8, 64], f32> {
  %res = mo.static.broadcast_to(%input) : !mo.tensor<[1, 64], f32> -> !mo.tensor<[8, 64], f32>
  mo.output %res : !mo.tensor<[8, 64], f32>
}

// Rank-expanding: in has one fewer dim than out (numpy semantics). The
// generated mogg.tensor.create.broadcast is identical in shape to the
// rank-preserving case above -- $outShape is the only shape this op carries;
// the input's own (smaller) rank is inferred later, purely from its Mojo
// argument type at emission time.

// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @broadcastRankExpanding
// CHECK: mogg.tensor.create.broadcast(%{{.*}}) {{.*}}outShape = #mosh<ape[8, 64]>{{.*}} : !mogg.tensor
mo.graph @broadcastRankExpanding(%input: !mo.tensor<[64], f32>)
    -> !mo.tensor<[8, 64], f32> {
  %res = mo.static.broadcast_to(%input) : !mo.tensor<[64], f32> -> !mo.tensor<[8, 64], f32>
  mo.output %res : !mo.tensor<[8, 64], f32>
}

// RUN: mo-opt %s --mogg-import-packages="mojo-pkg-paths=%kernel_api_test_lib" --mo-to-map --map-fuse-kernels --map-allocate-accumulating-buffers --map-to-mogg | FileCheck %s
// RUN: mo-opt %s --mogg-import-packages="mojo-pkg-paths=%kernel_api_test_lib" --mo-to-map --map-fuse-kernels --map-allocate-accumulating-buffers --map-to-mogg="enable-compute-lambdas=false" | FileCheck %s --check-prefix=NOCOMPUTE

// The GPU matmul declares its output as `_FusedComputeOutputTensor`, so an
// epilogue fused into it can be a COMPUTE lambda: the body yields the value the
// store would have written and the kernel performs the one store itself. The
// store-target capture (`%[[COUT]]`) survives unused -- emit still binds the
// functor onto its slice.
// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @matmul_add
// CHECK:       mogg.tensor.create.epilogue %{{[^ ]+}} (%[[VAL:[^ ]+]] : !mogg.simd<f32>, %[[IDX:[^ ]+]] : !map.index<2>) capturing {%[[COUT:[^ ]+]] = %{{[^ ]+}} : !mogg.tensor, %[[CZ:[^ ]+]] = %{{[^ ]+}} : !mogg.tensor} {{.*}}computeOutputArg = true
// CHECK-NEXT:    %[[ZV:.*]] = mogg.tensor.load %[[CZ]][%[[IDX]]]
// CHECK-NEXT:    %[[SUM:.*]] = mogg.call.elementwise @{{.*}}Add{{.*}}(%[[VAL]], %[[ZV]])
// CHECK-NEXT:    mogg.yield %[[SUM]] : !mogg.simd<f32>

// With compute lambdas off the same graph keeps a classic store lambda, but
// `computeOutputArg` still records what the kernel argument declares -- emit
// must bind through the compute entry point either way.
// NOCOMPUTE-LABEL: mo.graph @matmul_add
// NOCOMPUTE:       mogg.tensor.create.epilogue %{{[^ ]+}} (%{{[^ ]+}} : !mogg.simd<f32>, %[[IDX:[^ ,)]+]] : !map.index<2>) capturing {%[[COUT:[^ ,)]+]] = {{.*}}computeOutputArg = true
// NOCOMPUTE-NEXT:    mogg.tensor.load
// NOCOMPUTE-NEXT:    %[[SUM:.*]] = mogg.call.elementwise
// NOCOMPUTE-NEXT:    mogg.tensor.store %[[COUT]][%[[IDX]]] = %[[SUM]]
mo.graph @matmul_add(
  %a: !mo.tensor<[8, 8], f32, gpu:0>,
  %b: !mo.tensor<[8, 8], f32, gpu:0>,
  %z: !mo.tensor<[8, 8], f32, gpu:0>
) -> !mo.tensor<[8, 8], f32, gpu:0> {
  %mm = mo.matmul(%a, %b) : (!mo.tensor<[8, 8], f32, gpu:0>, !mo.tensor<[8, 8], f32, gpu:0>) -> !mo.tensor<[8, 8], f32, gpu:0>
  %out = mo.add(%mm, %z) : !mo.tensor<[8, 8], f32, gpu:0>
  mo.output %out : !mo.tensor<[8, 8], f32, gpu:0>
}

// A dtype-changing epilogue keeps a store lambda even though the kernel could
// take a compute one: `compute()` returns the dtype it was handed, so a body
// whose value leaves as si32 having arrived as f32 cannot round-trip through
// it. `computeOutputArg` is still set, because the kernel argument is still a
// `_FusedComputeOutputTensor`.
// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @mixed_dtype
// CHECK:       mogg.tensor.create.epilogue %{{[^ ]+}} (%[[V:[^ ]+]] : !mogg.simd<f32>, %[[I:[^ ]+]] : !map.index<2>) capturing {%[[CO:[^ ]+]] = {{.*}}computeOutputArg = true
// CHECK:         mogg.tensor.store %[[CO]][%[[I]]]
mo.graph @mixed_dtype(
  %a: !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>,
  %b: !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>,
  %bias: !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>
) -> !mo.tensor<[2, 2], si32> {
  %sum = mo.custom [symbol = "imposter_add_compute_fusion", device = #M.device_ref<"cpu", 0>](%a, %b) : (!mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>, !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>
  %added = mo.add(%sum, %bias) : !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>
  %out = mo.cast(%added) : (!mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[2, 2], si32>
  mo.output %out : !mo.tensor<[2, 2], si32>
}

// A store-only kernel argument is untouched: store lambda, and the attribute
// stays at its `false` default, which the printer elides. `computeOutputArg`
// sorts before `device`, so `device` following the output pointer immediately
// proves it is absent.
// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @plain_store
// CHECK:       mogg.tensor.create.epilogue %{{[^ ]+}} (%[[PV:[^ ]+]] : !mogg.simd<f32>, %[[PI:[^ ]+]] : !map.index<1>) capturing {%[[PO:[^ ]+]] = {{.*}} ptr %{{[^ ]+}} device =
// CHECK:         mogg.tensor.store %[[PO]][%[[PI]]]
mo.graph @plain_store(%a: !mo.tensor<[4], f32>, %b: !mo.tensor<[4], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[4], f32> {
  %c = mo.custom [symbol = "map_lower_one_fused_output", device = #M.device_ref<"cpu", 0>](%a) : (!mo.tensor<[4], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[4], f32>
  %out = mo.add(%c, %b) : !mo.tensor<[4], f32>
  mo.output %out : !mo.tensor<[4], f32>
}
GraphCompiler/test/mo-opt/Conversion/MAPToMOGG/dyn-opaque.mlir · complete source
// RUN: mo-opt %s --mogg-import-packages="mojo-pkg-paths=%kernel_api_test_lib" --mo-to-map --map-to-mogg | FileCheck %s

// Dynamic shapes: `mogg.routine` gains one `!mogg.dim` block argument per UNIQUE
// dynamic dimension (deduped across inputs and outputs), listed in the grouped
// header's `dims(...)` after `context(...)`, and each `mogg.shape.create` is fed
// the dims for its own tensor. The dim block arg keeps its source parameter name
// (`!mogg.dim<batch>`), but in the `shape.create` shape ATTR every dynamic dim is
// canonicalized to a single `dyn` placeholder (statics stay literal) so shapes
// that differ only in dim symbols dedup. Here the input and output share the
// dynamic dim `batch`, so there is exactly one `!mogg.dim<batch>` block arg and
// both `shape.create`s use it, each printing `#mosh<ape[dyn, 4]>`.

// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @dyn
// CHECK: mogg.routine (%{{.*}} : !mo.tensor<[batch, 4], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[batch, 4], f32>
// CHECK: inputs (%{{.*}})
// CHECK: outputs (%{{.*}})
// CHECK: context (%[[CTX:[^ ,)]+]])
// CHECK: dims (%[[D:.*]]: !mogg.dim<batch>) attributes {device = #M.device_ref<"cpu", 0>, fusionInfo = {{.*}}} {
// CHECK: mogg.shape.create(%[[D]]) <shape = #mosh<ape[dyn, 4]> : !mosh.ape> : !mogg.dim<batch>
// CHECK: mogg.shape.create(%[[D]]) <shape = #mosh<ape[dyn, 4]> : !mosh.ape> : !mogg.dim<batch>
// CHECK: mogg.call.opaque @{{.*}}MapLowerOnePlainOutput inputs(%{{.*}} : !mogg.tensor) outputs(%{{.*}} : !mogg.tensor) context(%[[CTX]] : !mogg.context)
mo.graph @dyn(%a: !mo.tensor<[batch, 4], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[batch, 4], f32> {
  %c = mo.custom [symbol = "map_lower_one_plain_output", device = #M.device_ref<"cpu", 0>](%a) : (!mo.tensor<[batch, 4], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[batch, 4], f32>
  mo.output %c : !mo.tensor<[batch, 4], f32>
}
GraphCompiler/test/mo-opt/Conversion/MAPToMOGG/fused-mutable-load-opaque.mlir · complete source
// RUN: mo-opt %s --mogg-import-packages="mojo-pkg-paths=%kernel_api_test_lib" --mo-to-map --map-pipeline --map-to-mogg | FileCheck %s
//
// And, after `ConformCallOperands`, the read-only operand is recreated immutable
// (this is the fix; without it the call would carry a mutable slice the kernel's
// immutable parameter rejects at codegen).
// RUN: mo-opt %s --mogg-import-packages="mojo-pkg-paths=%kernel_api_test_lib" --mo-to-map --map-pipeline --map-to-mogg --mogg-conform-call-operands | FileCheck %s --check-prefix=CONFORM

// `FuseMutableLoads` fuses a `mo.mutable.load` into an opaque kernel operand the
// kernel only reads -- here `map_lower_inplace_copy`'s immutable `src`. MAPToMOGG
// reconstructs every buffer operand as a mutable `mogg.tensor.create`
// (a `!mogg.buffer`), so both `dst` and the fused-read `src` come out mutable.
// `ConformCallOperands` then reconciles the read-only `src`: it accepts the
// mut->immut widening (OperandInference) and clones that operand's
// `mogg.tensor.create` immutable (`cloneWithMut`), yielding a `!mogg.tensor`
// whose codegen slice matches the kernel's `Input` parameter. `dst`, which the
// kernel genuinely writes, stays a mutable `!mogg.buffer`.

// Before conform: MAPToMOGG makes both operands mutable buffers.
// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @fused_mutable_load_into_immutable_input
// CHECK:     mogg.tensor.create({{.*}}) {{.*}}mut = true{{.*}}: !mogg.buffer
// CHECK:     mogg.tensor.create({{.*}}) {{.*}}mut = true{{.*}}: !mogg.buffer
// CHECK:     mogg.call.opaque @{{.*}}MapLowerInplaceCopy inputs(%{{.*}}, %{{.*}} : !mogg.buffer, !mogg.buffer)

// After conform: the read-only src is recreated immutable and the call uses it.
// CONFORM-LABEL: mo.graph @fused_mutable_load_into_immutable_input
// CONFORM:     mogg.tensor.create({{.*}}) {{.*}}mut = false{{.*}}: !mogg.tensor
// CONFORM:     mogg.call.opaque @{{.*}}MapLowerInplaceCopy inputs(%{{.*}}, %{{.*}} : !mogg.buffer, !mogg.tensor)
mo.graph @fused_mutable_load_into_immutable_input(%dst: !mo.buffer<[2, 2], f32>, %srcbuf: !mo.buffer<[2, 2], f32>) -> !mo.chain {
  %chain = mo.chain.create()
  %src, %loadchain = mo.mutable.load(%srcbuf, %chain) : (!mo.buffer<[2, 2], f32>, !mo.chain) -> (!mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>, !mo.chain)
  %outchain = mo.custom [symbol = "map_lower_inplace_copy", device = #M.device_ref<"cpu", 0>](%dst, %src, %chain) : (!mo.buffer<[2, 2], f32>, !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>, !mo.chain) -> !mo.chain
  mo.output %outchain : !mo.chain
}

// RUN: mo-opt %s --mogg-import-packages="mojo-pkg-paths=%kernel_api_test_lib" --mogg-rewrite-opaque-types --mo-to-map --map-to-mogg | FileCheck %s

// An `!mo.opaque` crosses a `mogg.routine` boundary as itself, not as a
// `!mogg.pointer` it is rebuilt from: it carries no shape, so there is
// nothing to reconstruct. Which side it sits on decides whether it gets a body
// block argument at all.
//
// As an INPUT it is destination-passing like a tensor, so it gets a block
// argument -- typed with the opaque itself, and passed straight to the call.
// As a RESULT it is not: the kernel allocates it internally and returns it, so
// there is no caller-allocated destination to point at. It gets no block
// argument, `mogg.call.opaque` grows a real result for it, and the kernel
// hands it out with `mogg.output`.
//
// Tensors keep their existing treatment throughout, so the consumer below
// shows both conventions side by side in one kernel.

// An opaque RESULT: no `inputs`/`outputs` groups at all, just the context.
// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @opaque_result
// CHECK: mogg.routine () -> !mo.opaque<"{{.*}}SIMDPair", {S0 = 4 : i64, S1 = 8 : i64}>
// CHECK-NOT: outputs (
// CHECK: context (%[[CTX:[^ ,)]+]])
// CHECK: %[[CALL:.*]] = mogg.call.opaque @{{.*}}MakeSimdPair[P0 = 4 : i64, P1 = 8 : i64] -> !mo.opaque<"{{.*}}SIMDPair", {S0 = 4 : i64, S1 = 8 : i64}>
// CHECK: mogg.output %[[CALL]] : !mo.opaque<"{{.*}}SIMDPair", {S0 = 4 : i64, S1 = 8 : i64}>
mo.graph @opaque_result() -> !mo.opaque<"SIMDPair", {S0 = 4, S1 = 8}> {
  %pair = mo.custom [symbol = "make_simd_pair", device = #M.device_ref<"cpu", 0>, parameters = {}] () : () -> (!mo.opaque<"SIMDPair", {S0 = 4, S1 = 8}>)
  mo.output %pair : !mo.opaque<"SIMDPair", {S0 = 4, S1 = 8}>
}

// An opaque INPUT beside a tensor output: the opaque is its own block arg and
// reaches the call directly, while the tensor still goes through
// `mogg.shape.create` / `mogg.tensor.create` from a pointer.
// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @opaque_input
// CHECK: mogg.routine (%{{.*}} : !mo.opaque<"{{.*}}SIMDPair", {S0 = 4 : i64, S1 = 8 : i64}>) -> !mo.tensor<[12], si32>
// CHECK: inputs (%[[IN:[^ ,)]+]]: !mo.opaque<"{{.*}}SIMDPair", {S0 = 4 : i64, S1 = 8 : i64}>)
// CHECK: outputs (%[[OP:[^ ,)]+]])
// CHECK: context (%[[CTX:[^ ,)]+]])
// CHECK: %[[SH:.*]] = mogg.shape.create() <shape = #mosh<ape[12]> : !mosh.ape>
// CHECK: %[[OT:.*]] = mogg.tensor.create(%[[OP]], %[[SH]]) {{.*}} : !mogg.tensor
// CHECK: mogg.call.opaque @{{.*}}ParameterizedOpaqueType[P0 = 4 : i64] inputs(%[[IN]] : !mo.opaque<"{{.*}}SIMDPair", {S0 = 4 : i64, S1 = 8 : i64}>) outputs(%[[OT]] : !mogg.tensor)
mo.graph @opaque_input(
    %pair: !mo.opaque<"SIMDPair", {S0 = 4, S1 = 8}>
) -> !mo.tensor<[12], si32> {
  %out = mo.custom [symbol = "kernel_with_parameterized_opaque", device = #M.device_ref<"cpu", 0>] (%pair) : (!mo.opaque<"SIMDPair", {S0 = 4, S1 = 8}>) -> (!mo.tensor<[12], si32>)
  mo.output %out : !mo.tensor<[12], si32>
}

// RUN: mo-opt %s --mogg-import-packages="mojo-pkg-paths=%kernel_api_test_lib" --mo-to-map --map-to-mogg | FileCheck %s

// MAPToMOGG lowers a plain-output `map.iter.opaque` into a `mogg.routine`:
// inputs stay `!mo.tensor` operands and outputs stay `!mo.tensor` results, but
// inside the body each tensor is reconstructed from a `!mogg.pointer` block
// argument via `mogg.shape.create` / `mogg.tensor.create` (each recording the
// kernel's `device`), and the kernel call becomes `mogg.call.opaque` wired to
// the body's trailing `!mogg.context`. The grouped `_kernel` header lists the
// pointer block args as `inputs(...) outputs(...) context(...)`. (Store-epilogue
// / fused outputs are deferred and not exercised here.)

// Single plain output.
// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @one_plain
// CHECK: mogg.routine (%[[A:.*]] : !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>
// CHECK: inputs (%[[IP:[^ ,)]+]])
// CHECK: outputs (%[[OP:[^ ,)]+]])
// CHECK: context (%[[CTX:[^ ,)]+]]) attributes {device = #M.device_ref<"cpu", 0>, fusionInfo = {{.*}}} {
// CHECK:   %[[ISH:.*]] = mogg.shape.create() <shape = #mosh<ape[2, 2]> : !mosh.ape>
// CHECK:   %[[IT:.*]] = mogg.tensor.create(%[[IP]], %[[ISH]]) <device = "cpu",{{.*}}mut = false{{.*}}> : !mogg.tensor
// CHECK:   %[[OSH:.*]] = mogg.shape.create() <shape = #mosh<ape[2, 2]> : !mosh.ape>
// CHECK:   %[[OT:.*]] = mogg.tensor.create(%[[OP]], %[[OSH]]) <device = "cpu",{{.*}}mut = true{{.*}}> : !mogg.tensor
// CHECK:   mogg.call.opaque @{{.*}}MapLowerOnePlainOutput inputs(%[[IT]] : !mogg.tensor) outputs(%[[OT]] : !mogg.tensor) context(%[[CTX]] : !mogg.context)
// Nothing is fused here, so the epilogue flag keeps its `false` default, which
// the printer elides -- its absence is the assertion.
// CHECK-NOT: hasEpilogueFusion
mo.graph @one_plain(%a: !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32> {
  %c = mo.custom [symbol = "map_lower_one_plain_output", device = #M.device_ref<"cpu", 0>](%a) : (!mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>
  mo.output %c : !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>
}

// Two plain outputs: one input pointer, two output pointers, one context.
// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @two_plain
// CHECK: mogg.routine (%{{.*}} : !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>) -> (!mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>, !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>)
// CHECK: inputs (%{{.*}})
// CHECK: outputs (%{{.*}}, %{{.*}})
// CHECK: context (%[[CTX:[^ ,)]+]]) attributes {device = #M.device_ref<"cpu", 0>, fusionInfo = {{.*}}} {
// CHECK:   mogg.call.opaque @{{.*}}MapLowerTwoPlainOutputs inputs(%{{.*}} : !mogg.tensor) outputs(%{{.*}}, %{{.*}} : !mogg.tensor, !mogg.tensor) context(%[[CTX]] : !mogg.context)
mo.graph @two_plain(%a: !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>) -> (!mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>, !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>) {
  %c:2 = mo.custom [symbol = "map_lower_two_plain_outputs", device = #M.device_ref<"cpu", 0>](%a) : (!mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>) -> (!mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>, !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>)
  mo.output %c#0, %c#1 : !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>, !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>
}
GraphCompiler/test/mo-opt/Conversion/MAPToMOGG/shape-func-kgen-params.mlir · complete source
// RUN: mo-opt %s --mogg-import-packages --mo-to-map --map-to-mogg | FileCheck %s

// mo.invoke_shape_func has no MAP form, so map-to-mogg lowers it directly. Its
// `kgenParams` are ordinary parameters of the shape function and must reach the
// call alongside the declared `output_rank`; forwarding only the rank leaves
// `axis` uninferable at emit time.

// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @gatherShapeFuncKgenParams
// CHECK: mogg.call.shape @{{.*}}gather_shape_fn
// CHECK-SAME: [axis = -2 : index, output_rank = 4 : index]
mo.graph @gatherShapeFuncKgenParams<() -> D0, D1, D2, D3>(
    %input: !mo.tensor<[1, 2, 3], f32>,
    %indices: !mo.tensor<[4, 5], f32>
) -> !mo.tensor<[D0, D1, D2, D3], si32> {
  mo.invoke_shape_func["mo.gather"]<() -> D4, D5, D6, D7>(%input, %indices)
    [kgenParams = {axis = -2 : index}, dataDeptTensors = []] :
    (!mo.tensor<[1, 2, 3], f32>, !mo.tensor<[4, 5], f32>)

  %one = mo.constant <#M.dense_array<1> : tensor<si32>> : !mo.tensor<[], si32>
  %val = mo.static.broadcast_to(%one): !mo.tensor<[], si32> -> !mo.tensor<[D4, D5, D6, D7], si32>

  mo.output<D4, D5, D6, D7> %val : !mo.tensor<[D4, D5, D6, D7], si32>
}
GraphCompiler/test/mo-opt/Conversion/MAPToMOGG/slice-stride.mlir · complete source
// RUN: mo-opt %s --pass-pipeline='builtin.module(mogg-import-packages, mo-to-map, map-outline-structured-kernel-bodies, mo.graph(map-livm, map.iter.opaque(canonicalize)), map-to-mogg)' | FileCheck %s

// Full pipeline from a real mo.slice op through MOToMAP, outlining, view
// motion, and MAPToMOGG: map.index.slice.stride lowers to
// mogg.tensor.create.slice, and only the slice result and the output tensor
// are captured by mogg.call.foreach, since the loop body only references
// those two. The `canonicalize` right after LoopInvariantViewMotion drops
// the closure's now-dead original captures (the raw input tensor and the
// starts/stops/steps bounds, all unused once the hoisted view replaces the
// load) via `DropDeadCapturingClosureCaptures` -- without it the lowered
// kernel's parameter list would carry those unused pointers too.

// Static bounds (mo.constant starts/stops/steps): every bound is a literal.

// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @sliceStaticBounds
// CHECK:       [[KERNEL:%[^ ]+]] = mogg.routine ({{.*}} : !mo.tensor<[10, 64], f32>, !mo.tensor<[2], si64>, !mo.tensor<[2], si64>, !mo.tensor<[2], si64>) -> !mo.tensor<[3, 32], f32>
// CHECK-NEXT:  inputs ([[IP0:%[^ :,]+]], [[IP1:%[^ :,]+]], [[IP2:%[^ :,]+]], [[IP3:%[^ :,]+]])
// CHECK-NEXT:  outputs ([[OP:%[^ :,]+]])
// CHECK-NEXT:  context ([[CTX:%[^ :,]+]]) attributes {device = #M.device_ref<"cpu", 0>, fusionInfo = {{.*}}} {
// CHECK-NEXT:    [[ISH0:%[^ ]+]] = mogg.shape.create() <shape = #mosh<ape[10, 64]> : !mosh.ape>
// CHECK-NEXT:    [[IT0:%[^ ]+]] = mogg.tensor.create([[IP0]], [[ISH0]]) {{.*}}io = Input{{.*}} : !mogg.tensor
// CHECK-NEXT:    [[ISH1:%[^ ]+]] = mogg.shape.create() <shape = #mosh<ape[2]> : !mosh.ape>
// CHECK-NEXT:    [[IT1:%[^ ]+]] = mogg.tensor.create([[IP1]], [[ISH1]]) {{.*}}io = Input{{.*}} : !mogg.tensor
// CHECK-NEXT:    [[ISH2:%[^ ]+]] = mogg.shape.create() <shape = #mosh<ape[2]> : !mosh.ape>
// CHECK-NEXT:    [[IT2:%[^ ]+]] = mogg.tensor.create([[IP2]], [[ISH2]]) {{.*}}io = Input{{.*}} : !mogg.tensor
// CHECK-NEXT:    [[ISH3:%[^ ]+]] = mogg.shape.create() <shape = #mosh<ape[2]> : !mosh.ape>
// CHECK-NEXT:    [[IT3:%[^ ]+]] = mogg.tensor.create([[IP3]], [[ISH3]]) {{.*}}io = Input{{.*}} : !mogg.tensor
// CHECK-NEXT:    [[OSH:%[^ ]+]] = mogg.shape.create() <shape = #mosh<ape[3, 32]> : !mosh.ape>
// CHECK-NEXT:    [[OT:%[^ ]+]] = mogg.tensor.create([[OP]], [[OSH]]) {{.*}}io = Output{{.*}} : !mogg.tensor
// CHECK-NEXT:    [[STRIDED:%[^ ]+]] = mogg.tensor.create.slice([[IT0]], [[IT1]], [[IT2]], [[IT3]]) {{.*}}outShape = #mosh<ape[3, 32]>{{.*}}staticStart = array<i64: 1, 32>{{.*}}staticStep = array<i64: 1, 1>{{.*}} : !mogg.tensor
// CHECK-NEXT:    [[LSH:%[^ ]+]] = mogg.shape.create() <shape = #mosh<ape[3, 32]> : !mosh.ape>
// CHECK-NEXT:    mogg.call.foreach @builtin_primitives.primitives._foreach shape([[LSH]]) context([[CTX]]) ([[IDX:%[^ :,]+]] : !map.index<2>) capturing {[[OUT:%[^ :,]+]] = [[OT]] : !mogg.tensor, [[STRIDEDARG:%[^ :,]+]] = [[STRIDED]] : !mogg.tensor} device = "cpu" {
// CHECK-NEXT:      [[VAL:%[^ ]+]] = mogg.tensor.load [[STRIDEDARG]]{{\[}}[[IDX]]] : !mogg.tensor, !map.index<2> -> !mogg.simd<f32>
// CHECK-NEXT:      mogg.tensor.store [[OUT]]{{\[}}[[IDX]]] = [[VAL]] : !mogg.tensor, !map.index<2>, !mogg.simd<f32>
// CHECK-NEXT:    }
// CHECK-NEXT:  }
mo.graph @sliceStaticBounds(%input: !mo.tensor<[10, 64], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[3, 32], f32> {
  %start = mo.constant <#M.dense_array<1, 32> : tensor<2xsi64>> : !mo.tensor<[2], si64>
  %stop = mo.constant <#M.dense_array<4, 64> : tensor<2xsi64>> : !mo.tensor<[2], si64>
  %step = mo.constant <#M.dense_array<1, 1> : tensor<2xsi64>> : !mo.tensor<[2], si64>
  %res = mo.slice(%input, %start, %stop, %step) : (
    !mo.tensor<[10, 64], f32>, !mo.tensor<[2], si64>, !mo.tensor<[2], si64>, !mo.tensor<[2], si64>
  ) -> !mo.tensor<[3, 32], f32>
  mo.output %res : !mo.tensor<[3, 32], f32>
}

// Dynamic bounds (graph arguments, not mo.constant): every bound is
// unresolved at compile time.

// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @sliceDynamicBounds
// CHECK: mogg.tensor.create.slice(%{{.*}}, %{{.*}}, %{{.*}}, %{{.*}}) {{.*}}outShape = #mosh<ape[3, 32]>{{.*}}
mo.graph @sliceDynamicBounds(
    %input: !mo.tensor<[10, 64], f32>,
    %start: !mo.tensor<[2], si64>,
    %stop: !mo.tensor<[2], si64>,
    %step: !mo.tensor<[2], si64>)
    -> !mo.tensor<[3, 32], f32> {
  %res = mo.slice(%input, %start, %stop, %step) : (
    !mo.tensor<[10, 64], f32>, !mo.tensor<[2], si64>, !mo.tensor<[2], si64>, !mo.tensor<[2], si64>
  ) -> !mo.tensor<[3, 32], f32>
  mo.output %res : !mo.tensor<[3, 32], f32>
}

// A constant start indexing a DYNAMIC input dim (mirrors `x[-8:]` off a
// dynamic `seq_len`): MOToMAP normalizes a start against its dim's extent only
// for static-input dims, so this start stays the raw literal `-8`. Its real
// offset `dim - 8` is not known until runtime, so its `staticStart` entry must
// lower to `?` (`kDynamic`, printed as the i64 min) -- not the raw `-8`, which
// the slice primitive cannot infer as a comptime offset (GEX-3964 / the
// mixed-shape LLM snifftest gap). The static dim1 start (0) stays static.

// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @sliceNegativeStartDynamicInDim
// CHECK: mogg.tensor.create.slice(%{{.*}}, %{{.*}}, %{{.*}}, %{{.*}}) {{.*}}staticStart = array<i64: -9223372036854775808, 0>{{.*}}staticStep = array<i64: 1, 1>{{.*}}
mo.graph @sliceNegativeStartDynamicInDim(
    %input: !mo.tensor<[?, 64], f32>,
    %stop: !mo.tensor<[2], si64>)
    -> !mo.tensor<[?, 64], f32> {
  %start = mo.constant <#M.dense_array<-8, 0> : tensor<2xsi64>> : !mo.tensor<[2], si64>
  %step = mo.constant <#M.dense_array<1, 1> : tensor<2xsi64>> : !mo.tensor<[2], si64>
  %res = mo.slice(%input, %start, %stop, %step) : (
    !mo.tensor<[?, 64], f32>, !mo.tensor<[2], si64>, !mo.tensor<[2], si64>, !mo.tensor<[2], si64>
  ) -> !mo.tensor<[?, 64], f32>
  mo.output %res : !mo.tensor<[?, 64], f32>
}

// A NON-negative constant start indexing a DYNAMIC input dim: `2` is already an
// absolute offset (no extent needed to resolve it), so it stays a comptime
// `staticStart` hint even though dim0 is dynamic -- only negatives, which need
// the unknown extent to normalize, must lower to `?`.

// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @slicePositiveStartDynamicInDim
// CHECK: mogg.tensor.create.slice(%{{.*}}, %{{.*}}, %{{.*}}, %{{.*}}) {{.*}}staticStart = array<i64: 2, 0>{{.*}}staticStep = array<i64: 1, 1>{{.*}}
mo.graph @slicePositiveStartDynamicInDim(
    %input: !mo.tensor<[?, 64], f32>,
    %stop: !mo.tensor<[2], si64>)
    -> !mo.tensor<[?, 64], f32> {
  %start = mo.constant <#M.dense_array<2, 0> : tensor<2xsi64>> : !mo.tensor<[2], si64>
  %step = mo.constant <#M.dense_array<1, 1> : tensor<2xsi64>> : !mo.tensor<[2], si64>
  %res = mo.slice(%input, %start, %stop, %step) : (
    !mo.tensor<[?, 64], f32>, !mo.tensor<[2], si64>, !mo.tensor<[2], si64>, !mo.tensor<[2], si64>
  ) -> !mo.tensor<[?, 64], f32>
  mo.output %res : !mo.tensor<[?, 64], f32>
}
GraphCompiler/test/mo-opt/Conversion/MAPToMOGG/transpose-reduce-dynamic-dim.mlir · complete source
// RUN: rm -rf %t && mkdir -p %t
// RUN: env MODULAR_DEBUG=ir-output-dir=%t mo-opt %s \
// RUN:   --mo-shape-inference --gc-pipeline=constant-fold=false -o /dev/null
// RUN: cat %t/*.mogg-pre-mgp.mlir | FileCheck %s

// A dynamic-permutation transpose fused into a dim-reducing consumer (reduce
// over the transposed last axis). The transposed view's reduced axis (D11) is
// a fresh runtime symbol that appears on no kernel-boundary tensor -- only on
// the intermediate view and the fused prologue's own shape. Kernel dynamic-dim
// collection walks every op in the body (not just the I/O signature), so D11
// still gets a `!mogg.dim` handle and the prologue's `mogg.shape.create`
// lowers instead of dereferencing a null dim. This is the compile-side
// regression guard for that collection; the end-to-end run stays excluded on a
// separate strided-view-through-prologue value bug.

// CHECK: mogg.tensor.create.transpose
// The rowwise iteration shape for the reduce input carries all four
// transposed dims, including the reduced axis D11 that lives only on the
// intermediate view.
// CHECK: %[[SHAPE:.*]] = mogg.shape.create({{.*}}) <shape = #mosh<ape[dyn, dyn, dyn, dyn]>{{.*}} : !mogg.dim<D8>, !mogg.dim<D9>, !mogg.dim<D10>, !mogg.dim<D11>
// CHECK-NEXT: mogg.with_trace {
// CHECK-NEXT: mogg.call.rowwise shape(%[[SHAPE]]) axis(3)

mo.graph @serving_default<D0, D1, D2, D3 -> D4, D5, D6>(%arg0: !mo.tensor<[D0, D1, D2, D3], f32>, %arg1: !mo.tensor<[4], si32>) -> !mo.tensor<[D4, D5, D6, 1], f32> attributes {argument_names = ["input_1", "input_2"], result_names = ["lambda"]} {
  %0 = mo.transpose<() -> D8, D9, D10, D11>(%arg0, %arg1) : (!mo.tensor<[D0, D1, D2, D3], f32>, !mo.tensor<[4], si32>) -> !mo.tensor<[D8, D9, D10, D11], f32>
  %1 = mo.reduce.add(%0) : (!mo.tensor<[D8, D9, D10, D11], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[D8, D9, D10, 1], f32>
  mo.output<D8, D9, D10> %1 : !mo.tensor<[D8, D9, D10, 1], f32>
}
GraphCompiler/test/mo-opt/Conversion/MAPToMOGG/transpose-stride.mlir · complete source
// RUN: mo-opt %s --pass-pipeline='builtin.module(mogg-import-packages, mo-to-map, map-outline-structured-kernel-bodies, mo.graph(map-livm, map.iter.opaque(canonicalize)), map-to-mogg)' | FileCheck %s

// Full pipeline from a real mo.transpose op through MOToMAP, outlining, view
// motion, and MAPToMOGG: map.index.transpose.stride lowers to
// mogg.tensor.create.transpose, which carries the view's own output shape and
// the compile-time-known part of the perm (`staticPermutations`) -- the input's
// shape/rank is read off the input tensor operand at Mojo-emission time, not
// duplicated onto this op. perm rides in as a runtime tensor operand too
// (reconstructed as mogg.tensor.create like any other kernel input); a
// constant perm never reads it at runtime, but it stays live because the view
// primitive takes it. The `canonicalize` right after LoopInvariantViewMotion
// drops the closure's now-dead original input capture (unused once the
// hoisted transpose view replaces the load) via
// `DropDeadCapturingClosureCaptures`.

// 2D swap: out.dim[0] = in.dim[1], out.dim[1] = in.dim[0].

// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @transposeSwap
// CHECK:       [[KERNEL:%[^ ]+]] = mogg.routine {{(dispatch\([a-z]+\) )?}}({{.*}} : !mo.tensor<[2, 3], f32>, !mo.tensor<[2], si64>) -> !mo.tensor<[3, 2], f32>
// CHECK-NEXT:  inputs ([[IP:%[^ :,]+]], [[PP:%[^ :,]+]])
// CHECK-NEXT:  outputs ([[OP:%[^ :,]+]])
// CHECK-NEXT:  context ([[CTX:%[^ :,]+]]) attributes {device = #M.device_ref<"cpu", 0>, fusionInfo = {{.*}}} {
// CHECK-NEXT:    [[ISH:%[^ ]+]] = mogg.shape.create() <shape = #mosh<ape[2, 3]> : !mosh.ape>
// CHECK-NEXT:    [[IT:%[^ ]+]] = mogg.tensor.create([[IP]], [[ISH]]) {{.*}}io = Input{{.*}} : !mogg.tensor
// CHECK-NEXT:    [[PSH:%[^ ]+]] = mogg.shape.create() <shape = #mosh<ape[2]> : !mosh.ape>
// CHECK-NEXT:    [[PT:%[^ ]+]] = mogg.tensor.create([[PP]], [[PSH]]) {{.*}}io = Input{{.*}} : !mogg.tensor
// CHECK-NEXT:    [[OSH:%[^ ]+]] = mogg.shape.create() <shape = #mosh<ape[3, 2]> : !mosh.ape>
// CHECK-NEXT:    [[OT:%[^ ]+]] = mogg.tensor.create([[OP]], [[OSH]]) {{.*}}io = Output{{.*}} : !mogg.tensor
// CHECK-NEXT:    [[TRANS:%[^ ]+]] = mogg.tensor.create.transpose([[IT]], [[PT]]) {{.*}}outShape = #mosh<ape[3, 2]>{{.*}}staticPermutations = array<i64: 1, 0>{{.*}} : !mogg.tensor
// CHECK-NEXT:    [[LSH:%[^ ]+]] = mogg.shape.create() <shape = #mosh<ape[3, 2]> : !mosh.ape>
// CHECK-NEXT:    mogg.call.foreach @builtin_primitives.primitives._foreach shape([[LSH]]) context([[CTX]]) ([[IDX:%[^ :,]+]] : !map.index<2>) capturing {[[OUT:%[^ :,]+]] = [[OT]] : !mogg.tensor, [[TRANSARG:%[^ :,]+]] = [[TRANS]] : !mogg.tensor} device = "cpu" {
// CHECK-NEXT:      [[VAL:%[^ ]+]] = mogg.tensor.load [[TRANSARG]]{{\[}}[[IDX]]] : !mogg.tensor, !map.index<2> -> !mogg.simd<f32>
// CHECK-NEXT:      mogg.tensor.store [[OUT]]{{\[}}[[IDX]]] = [[VAL]] : !mogg.tensor, !map.index<2>, !mogg.simd<f32>
// CHECK-NEXT:    }
// CHECK-NEXT:  }
mo.graph @transposeSwap(%input: !mo.tensor<[2, 3], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[3, 2], f32> {
  %perm = mo.constant <#M.dense_array<1, 0> : tensor<2xsi64>> : !mo.tensor<[2], si64>
  %res = mo.transpose(%input, %perm) : (
    !mo.tensor<[2, 3], f32>, !mo.tensor<[2], si64>
  ) -> !mo.tensor<[3, 2], f32>
  mo.output %res : !mo.tensor<[3, 2], f32>
}

// 3D permutation: the generated mogg.tensor.create.transpose carries the
// full non-trivial perm; the input's own (differently-ordered) shape is
// inferred later, purely from its Mojo argument type at emission time.

// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @transpose3D
// CHECK: mogg.tensor.create.transpose(%{{.*}}, %{{.*}}) {{.*}}outShape = #mosh<ape[4, 2, 3]>{{.*}}staticPermutations = array<i64: 2, 0, 1>{{.*}} : !mogg.tensor
mo.graph @transpose3D(%input: !mo.tensor<[2, 3, 4], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[4, 2, 3], f32> {
  %perm = mo.constant <#M.dense_array<2, 0, 1> : tensor<3xsi64>> : !mo.tensor<[3], si64>
  %res = mo.transpose(%input, %perm) : (
    !mo.tensor<[2, 3, 4], f32>, !mo.tensor<[3], si64>
  ) -> !mo.tensor<[4, 2, 3], f32>
  mo.output %res : !mo.tensor<[4, 2, 3], f32>
}

// RUN: mo-opt %s --mogg-import-packages="mojo-pkg-paths=%kernel_api_test_lib" --mo-to-map --map-allocate-accumulating-buffers --map-to-mogg --mogg-outline-routines | FileCheck %s

// OutlineRoutines moves each `mogg.routine` body into a module-level
// `mogg.func` labeled with the MOGG ABI, and replaces the kernel body
// with a single `mogg.call` forwarding the pointer / dim / context block
// args. The `mogg.routine` container is kept for `MOGGToMGP`.
//
// The stub is named `__<ops it fuses>`; two kernels that fuse the same ops share
// a preferred name, so the symbol table appends a numeric suffix to the second
// (`..._0`), as `@dyn` and `@one_plain` show below.

// Plain output: the kernel body becomes one `mogg.call`; the shape/tensor
// reconstruction + `mogg.call.opaque` move into the MAP-ABI stub.
// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @one_plain
// CHECK: mogg.routine (%{{.*}} : !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>
// CHECK:   inputs (%[[IP:[^ ,)]+]])
// CHECK:   outputs (%[[OP:[^ ,)]+]])
// CHECK:   context (%[[C:[^ ,)]+]]) attributes {device = #M.device_ref<"cpu", 0>, fusionInfo = {{.*}}} {
// CHECK:     mogg.call @[[STUB0:__[A-Za-z0-9_]+]] %[[IP]], %[[OP]], %[[C]] : !mogg.pointer, !mogg.pointer, !mogg.context
// CHECK-NOT: mogg.call.opaque
// CHECK: mogg.func @[[STUB0]] private (%{{.*}}: !mogg.pointer, %{{.*}}: !mogg.pointer, %{{.*}}: !mogg.context) attributes {abi = #mogg.abi<MOGG>,
// CHECK:   %[[ISH:.*]] = mogg.shape.create() {{.*}}{{$}}
// CHECK:   %[[IT:.*]] = mogg.tensor.create(%{{.*}}, %[[ISH]]) {{.*}}mut = false{{.*}} : !mogg.tensor
// CHECK:   %[[OT:.*]] = mogg.tensor.create(%{{.*}}, %{{.*}}) {{.*}}mut = true{{.*}} : !mogg.tensor
// CHECK:   mogg.call.opaque @{{.*}}MapLowerOnePlainOutput inputs(%[[IT]] : !mogg.tensor) outputs(%[[OT]] : !mogg.tensor) context(%{{.*}} : !mogg.context)
// CHECK:   mogg.output
mo.graph @one_plain(%a: !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32> {
  %c = mo.custom [symbol = "map_lower_one_plain_output", device = #M.device_ref<"cpu", 0>](%a) : (!mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>
  mo.output %c : !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>
}

// Fused output: the epilogue lambda + `mogg.tensor.create.epilogue` ride inside
// the stub body alongside the call.
// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @one_fused
// CHECK:   inputs (%[[IP:[^ ,)]+]])
// CHECK:   outputs (%[[OP:[^ ,)]+]])
// CHECK:   context (%[[C:[^ ,)]+]]) attributes {device = #M.device_ref<"cpu", 0>, fusionInfo = {{.*}}} {
// CHECK:     mogg.call @[[STUB1:__[A-Za-z0-9_]+]] %[[IP]], %[[OP]], %[[C]] : !mogg.pointer, !mogg.pointer, !mogg.context
// CHECK: mogg.func @[[STUB1]] private {{.*}} attributes {abi = #mogg.abi<MOGG>,
// CHECK:   %{{.*}} = mogg.tensor.create.epilogue %{{.*}} (%{{.*}} : !mogg.simd<f32>, %{{.*}} : !map.index<2>) capturing {%[[CAP:[^ ,)]+]] = %{{.*}} : !mogg.tensor} ptr %{{.*}} {{.*}} {
// CHECK:     mogg.tensor.store %[[CAP]][%{{.*}}] = %{{.*}}
// CHECK:   }
// CHECK:   mogg.call.opaque @{{.*}}MapLowerOneFusedOutput
// CHECK:   mogg.output
mo.graph @one_fused(%a: !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32> {
  %c = mo.custom [symbol = "map_lower_one_fused_output", device = #M.device_ref<"cpu", 0>](%a) : (!mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>
  mo.output %c : !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>
}

// Dynamic dim: the `!mogg.dim` block arg is forwarded through the call.stub into
// the stub signature, where `mogg.shape.create` consumes it.
// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @dyn
// CHECK:   inputs (%[[IP:[^ ,)]+]])
// CHECK:   outputs (%[[OP:[^ ,)]+]])
// CHECK:   context (%[[C:[^ ,)]+]])
// CHECK:   dims (%[[D:.*]]: !mogg.dim<batch>) attributes {device = #M.device_ref<"cpu", 0>, fusionInfo = {{.*}}} {
// CHECK:     mogg.call @[[STUB2:__[A-Za-z0-9_]+]] %[[IP]], %[[OP]], %[[D]], %[[C]] : !mogg.pointer, !mogg.pointer, !mogg.dim<batch>, !mogg.context
// CHECK: mogg.func @[[STUB2]] private (%{{.*}}: !mogg.pointer, %{{.*}}: !mogg.pointer, %[[SD:.*]]: !mogg.dim<batch>, %{{.*}}: !mogg.context) attributes {abi = #mogg.abi<MOGG>,
// CHECK:   mogg.shape.create(%[[SD]]) {{.*}} : !mogg.dim<batch>
mo.graph @dyn(%a: !mo.tensor<[batch, 4], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[batch, 4], f32> {
  %c = mo.custom [symbol = "map_lower_one_plain_output", device = #M.device_ref<"cpu", 0>](%a) : (!mo.tensor<[batch, 4], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[batch, 4], f32>
  mo.output %c : !mo.tensor<[batch, 4], f32>
}

from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
from max.driver import CPU, Accelerator, Buffer, accelerator_count
from max.dtype import DType
from max.engine.api import InferenceSession
from max.graph import DeviceRef, Graph, TensorType, ops


def main() -> None:
    mojo_kernels = Path(__file__).parent / "kernels"

    dtype = DType.float32

    # Place the graph on a GPU, if available. Fall back to CPU if not.
    device = CPU() if accelerator_count() == 0 else Accelerator()
    if accelerator_count() == 0:
        N = 8
        D = 8
        BD = 4
        BN = 4
    else:
        N = 32
        D = 32
        BD = 8
        BN = 16

    with Graph(
        "fused_attention",
        input_types=[
            TensorType(
                dtype, shape=[N, D], device=DeviceRef.from_device(device)
            ),
            TensorType(
                dtype, shape=[N, D], device=DeviceRef.from_device(device)
            ),
            TensorType(
                dtype, shape=[N, D], device=DeviceRef.from_device(device)
            ),
        ],
        custom_extensions=[mojo_kernels],
    ) as graph:
        q, k, v, *_ = graph.inputs
        results = ops.custom(
            name="modular_ops::fused_attention_custom",
            device=DeviceRef.from_device(device),
            parameters={"BD": BD, "BN": BN},
            values=[q, k, v],
            out_types=[
                TensorType(
                    dtype, shape=[N, D], device=DeviceRef.from_device(device)
                )
            ],
        )
        graph.output(*results)

    # Set up an inference session for running the graph.
    session = InferenceSession(devices=[device])

    # Compile the graph.
    compiled = session.compile(graph)
    model = session.init(compiled)

    np.random.seed(123)
    Q = Buffer.from_numpy(np.random.randn(N, D).astype("f")).to(device)
    K = Buffer.from_numpy(np.random.randn(N, D).astype("f")).to(device)
    V = Buffer.from_numpy(np.random.randn(N, D).astype("f")).to(device)

    output = model.execute(Q, K, V)
    print(output)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""
The code below computes the attention score for a tile of size BN x BD.
It follows the exact arithmetic as described in the FlashAttention-2 paper
(https://arxiv.org/pdf/2307.08691). The variable names in this program
reflect the variable names in the algorithms from the paper.

Here, the following tensors are Q for the query,
K for the key, V for the value, and O for the output.

       Q            K               V
  +----D----+  +----D----+   +--+--BD--+---+
  |         |  |.........|   |  |......|   |
  |         |  |.........|   |  |......|   |
  +---------+  |.........|   |  |......|   |
  |.........|  |.........|   |  |......|   |
  BN........|  N.........|   N  |......|   |
  |.........|  |.........|   |  |......|   |
  +---------+  |.........|   |  |......|   |
  |         |  |.........|   |  |......|   |
  |         |  |.........|   |  |......|   |
  |         |  |.........|   |  |......|   |
  +---------+  +---------+   +--+------+---+

The main trick is in the softmax computation.
As the paper says, S and P are intermediate values.

Let S = Q * K^T  ∈ R^{N, D}
    P = Softmax(S) ∈ R^{N, D}
The attention score is O = P * V ∈ R^{N, D}.

One way to think about this is to consider what happens if we
split the dimensions N in  K, and Q into two tiles: K_1 and K_2, V_1 and V_2.
Then we can incrementally compute the output as follows:
  S_1 = Q * K_1, S_2 = Q * K_2
  O_i = O_{i-1} * renormalization_factor + softmax(S_i) * V_i

This allows for the incremental computation of softmax(S_i) * V_i,
leading to the final output.
"""


from max.gpu.host import DeviceContext
from max.gpu import block_idx
from max.gpu.sync import barrier
from layout import TensorLayout, TileTensor, row_major, stack_allocation
from layout.math import max, sum
from layout.tensor_core import TensorCore

from extensibility import register, InputTensor, OutputTensor

from std.utils import Index


@register("modular_ops::fused_attention_custom")
struct FusedAttention:
    """Registers the `fused_attention_custom` op, allowing python to use it from the `max`
    package.
    """

    @staticmethod
    def execute[
        dtype: DType,
        rank: Int,
        //,  # Forces the previous two params to be inferred from the args
        BN: Int,  # Dimension of blocks to split Q into
        BD: Int,  # Dimension of blocks to split K, V into
        target: StaticString,  # "cpu" or "gpu"
    ](
        output: OutputTensor[dtype=dtype, rank=rank, ...],
        query: InputTensor[dtype=dtype, rank=rank, ...],
        key: InputTensor[dtype=dtype, rank=rank, ...],
        value: InputTensor[dtype=dtype, rank=rank, ...],
        ctx: DeviceContext,
    ) raises:
        comptime assert rank == 2, "rank must be 2"

        # Query tensor
        var Q = query.to_tile_tensor().as_unsafe_any_origin()
        # Key tensor
        var K = key.to_tile_tensor().as_unsafe_any_origin()
        # Value tensor
        var V = value.to_tile_tensor().as_unsafe_any_origin()
        # Attention output tensor
        var O = output.to_tile_tensor().as_unsafe_any_origin()

        comptime if target == "cpu":
            print("Running on CPU")
            fused_attention_cpu[BN, BD](Q, K, V, O)
        else:
            var dev_ctx = ctx
            print("Running on GPU")
            fused_attention_gpu[BN, BD](dev_ctx, Q, K, V, O)


# CustomOpLibrary does not support names with '::' in them currently. Create
# a simple alias so the whisper example works.
@register("fused_attention_custom")
struct FusedAttentionAlias:
    @staticmethod
    def execute[
        dtype: DType,
        rank: Int,
        //,  # Forces the previous two params to be inferred from the args
        BN: Int,  # Dimension of blocks to split Q into
        BD: Int,  # Dimension of blocks to split K, V into
        target: StaticString,  # "cpu" or "gpu"
    ](
        output: OutputTensor[dtype=dtype, rank=rank, ...],
        query: InputTensor[dtype=dtype, rank=rank, ...],
        key: InputTensor[dtype=dtype, rank=rank, ...],
        value: InputTensor[dtype=dtype, rank=rank, ...],
        ctx: DeviceContext,
    ) raises:
        FusedAttention.execute[BN=BN, BD=BD, target=target](
            output, query, key, value, ctx
        )


@inline(.always)
def matmul_b_transpose(
    lhs: TileTensor,
    rhs: TileTensor,
    out res: TileTensor[
        lhs.dtype,
        type_of(row_major[lhs.static_shape[0], rhs.static_shape[0]]()),
        MutUntrackedOrigin,
    ],
):
    res = stack_allocation[lhs.dtype](
        row_major[lhs.static_shape[0], rhs.static_shape[0]]()
    )

    comptime for m in range(lhs.static_shape[0]):
        comptime for n in range(rhs.static_shape[0]):
            res[m, n] = 0.0

            comptime for k in range(lhs.static_shape[1]):
                res[m, n] += rebind[res.ElementType](
                    lhs[m, k].cast[res.dtype]()
                ) * rebind[res.ElementType](rhs[n, k].cast[res.dtype]())


# The bulk of the code below implements what the papers calls
# an "online softmax", which is local to each block.
# The algorithm is described as:
#
# $$$
# m_1 = rowmax(S_1)
# l_1 = rowsum(e^(S_1-m_1))
# P_1 = diag(l_1)^-1 * e^(S_1-m_1)
# O_1 = P_1*V_1 = diag(l_1)^-1 * e^(S_1-m_1) * V_1
# m_2 = max(m_1, rowmax(S_2)) = m
# l_2 = e^(m_1-m_2) * l_1 _ rowsum(e^(S_2-m_2))
#     = rowsum(e^(S_1-m)) + rowsum(e^(S_2-m)) = ls
# P_2 = diag(l_2)^-1 * e^(S_2-m_2)
# O_2 = diag(l_1/l_2)^-1 * O_1 + (P_2 * V_2)
#     = diag(l_2)^-1 * e^(S_2-m) * V
# $$$


@inline(.always)
def fused_attention_cpu[
    BN: Int, BD: Int
](Q: TileTensor, K: TileTensor, V: TileTensor, O: TileTensor[mut=True, ...],):
    comptime N = K.static_shape[0]
    comptime D = K.static_shape[1]

    comptime for tile_n in range(N // BN):
        var Q_tile = Q.tile[BN, D](tile_n, 0)

        comptime for tile_d in range(D // BD):
            var m_1 = stack_allocation[Q.dtype](row_major[BN]()).fill(
                Scalar[Q.dtype].MIN
            )

            var l_1 = stack_allocation[Q.dtype](row_major[BN]()).fill(0)

            var O_i = stack_allocation[Q.dtype](row_major[BN, BD]()).fill(0)

            comptime for tile_n_idx in range(N // BN):
                var K_tile = K.tile[BN, D](tile_n_idx, 0)
                var V_tile = V.tile[BN, BD](tile_n_idx, tile_d)

                var S = matmul_b_transpose(Q_tile, K_tile)
                var m_2 = stack_allocation[Q.dtype](row_major[BN]())
                max[axis=1](S, m_2)
                m_2.max(m_1)

                # l_2 = exp(m_1 - m_2) * l_1 + sum(axis=1, exp(S - m_2))
                var l_2 = stack_allocation[Q.dtype](row_major[BN]())
                l_2.copy_from(m_1)
                l_2 -= m_2
                l_2.exp()
                l_2 *= l_1
                var E = stack_allocation[Q.dtype](row_major[BN, BN]())
                E.copy_from(S)
                E -= m_2
                E.exp()
                var l_2_sum = stack_allocation[Q.dtype](row_major[BN]())
                sum[axis=1](E, l_2_sum)
                l_2 += l_2_sum

                # P = exp(S - m_2) / l_2
                E /= l_2
                O_i *= l_1
                O_i /= l_2
                var m_1_delta = stack_allocation[Q.dtype](row_major[BN]())
                m_1_delta.copy_from(m_1)
                m_1_delta -= m_2
                m_1_delta.exp()
                O_i *= m_1_delta
                var PV = matmul["cpu"](E, V_tile)
                O_i += PV
                m_1.copy_from(m_2)
                l_1.copy_from(l_2)

            O.tile[BN, BD](tile_n, tile_d).copy_from(O_i)


@inline(.always)
def matmul[
    dtype: DType,
    rhs_dtype: DType,
    //,
    target: StaticString,
    transpose_b: Bool = False,
](
    lhs: TileTensor[dtype, ...],
    rhs: TileTensor[rhs_dtype, ...],
    out res: TileTensor[
        dtype,
        type_of(row_major[lhs.static_shape[0], rhs.static_shape[0]]()),
        MutUntrackedOrigin,
        address_space=lhs.address_space,
    ],
):
    res = stack_allocation[dtype, address_space=lhs.address_space](
        row_major[lhs.static_shape[0], rhs.static_shape[0]]()
    )

    comptime if target == "cpu":
        comptime for m in range(lhs.static_shape[0]):
            comptime for n in range(rhs.static_shape[1]):
                res[m, n] = 0.0

                comptime for k in range(lhs.static_shape[1]):
                    res[m, n] += rebind[res.ElementType](
                        lhs[m, k].cast[res.dtype]()
                    ) * rebind[res.ElementType](rhs[k, n].cast[res.dtype]())
    else:
        comptime M = lhs.static_shape[0]
        comptime N = rhs.static_shape[0]
        comptime K = lhs.static_shape[1]

        var out_sram = stack_allocation[res.dtype, address_space=.SHARED](
            row_major[M, N]()
        )

        comptime BK = 8

        comptime assert K % 8 == 0, "K needs to be a multiple of 8"

        var mma_b_t = TensorCore[dtype, dtype, Index(M, N, BK), transpose_b]()

        var c_reg = stack_allocation[dtype, address_space=.LOCAL](
            mma_b_t.c_fragment_layout
        ).fill(0)

        # `TensorCore`'s native loads require matching operand dtypes;
        # rebind the B view once when `rhs` carries a different dtype.
        var rhs_typed = rebind[
            TileTensor[
                dtype,
                rhs.LayoutType,
                rhs.origin,
                Engine=rhs.Engine,
                address_space=rhs.address_space,
                linear_idx_type=rhs.linear_idx_type,
            ]
        ](rhs)

        comptime for k_i in range(K // BK):
            var a_reg = mma_b_t.load_a(lhs.tile[M, BK](0, k_i))

            var b_reg = mma_b_t.load_b(rhs_typed.tile[BK, N](k_i, 0))

            comptime if transpose_b:
                b_reg = rebind[type_of(b_reg)](
                    mma_b_t.load_b(rhs_typed.tile[N, BK](0, k_i))
                )

            var d_reg = mma_b_t.mma_op(a_reg, b_reg, c_reg)
            c_reg.copy_from(d_reg)
        mma_b_t.store_d(out_sram, c_reg)

        barrier()
        res.copy_from(out_sram)


def fused_attention_kernel[
    q_dtype: DType,
    q_layout: TensorLayout,
    k_dtype: DType,
    k_layout: TensorLayout,
    v_dtype: DType,
    v_layout: TensorLayout,
    o_dtype: DType,
    o_layout: TensorLayout,
    BN: Int,
    BD: Int,
](
    Q: TileTensor[q_dtype, q_layout, MutAnyOrigin],
    K: TileTensor[k_dtype, k_layout, MutAnyOrigin],
    V: TileTensor[v_dtype, v_layout, MutAnyOrigin],
    O: TileTensor[o_dtype, o_layout, MutAnyOrigin],
):
    comptime N = Q.static_shape[0]
    comptime D = Q.static_shape[1]

    var Q_tile = Q.tile[BN, D](block_idx.y, 0)

    var m_1 = stack_allocation[q_dtype](row_major[BN]()).fill(
        Scalar[q_dtype].MIN
    )
    var l_1 = stack_allocation[q_dtype](row_major[BN]()).fill(0)
    var O_i = stack_allocation[q_dtype](row_major[BN, BD]()).fill(0)

    comptime BN_1 = 8

    for tile_n_idx in range(N // BN_1):
        var K_tile = K.tile[BN_1, D](tile_n_idx, 0)
        var V_tile = V.tile[BN_1, BD](tile_n_idx, block_idx.x)
        var S = matmul["gpu", transpose_b=True](Q_tile, K_tile)
        var m_2 = stack_allocation[q_dtype](row_major[BN]())
        max[axis=1](S, m_2)
        m_2.max(m_1)

        # l_2 = exp(m_1 - m_2) * l_1 + sum(axis=1, exp(S - m_2))
        var l_2 = stack_allocation[q_dtype](row_major[BN]())
        l_2.copy_from(m_1)
        l_2 -= m_2
        l_2.exp()
        l_2 *= l_1
        var E = stack_allocation[q_dtype](row_major[BN, BN_1]())
        E.copy_from(S)
        E -= m_2
        E.exp()
        var l_2_sum = stack_allocation[q_dtype](row_major[BN]())
        sum[axis=1](E, l_2_sum)
        l_2 += l_2_sum

        # P = exp(S - m_2) / l_2
        E /= l_2
        O_i *= l_1
        O_i /= l_2
        var m_1_delta = stack_allocation[q_dtype](row_major[BN]())
        m_1_delta.copy_from(m_1)
        m_1_delta -= m_2
        m_1_delta.exp()
        O_i *= m_1_delta
        var PV = matmul["gpu"](E, V_tile)
        O_i += PV
        m_1.copy_from(m_2)
        l_1.copy_from(l_2)
    O.tile[BN, BD](block_idx.y, block_idx.x).copy_from(O_i)


def fused_attention_gpu[
    BN: Int,
    BD: Int,
](
    ctx: DeviceContext,
    Q: TileTensor,
    K: TileTensor,
    V: TileTensor,
    O: TileTensor[mut=True, ...],
) raises:
    comptime kernel_func = fused_attention_kernel[
        Q.dtype,
        Q.LayoutType,
        K.dtype,
        K.LayoutType,
        V.dtype,
        V.LayoutType,
        O.dtype,
        O.LayoutType,
        BN,
        BD,
    ]
    ctx.enqueue_function[kernel_func](
        Q,
        K,
        V,
        O,
        grid_dim=(Int(Q.dim[1]()) // BD, Int(Q.dim[0]()) // BN),
        block_dim=(32),
    )
